findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to trigger.expect regardless of posture. The reference FlowRunStateTriggerFields (flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx:24-25) and the new DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:30-31) both switch to trigger.after when posture is Proactive ('Stays in'), and the stories encode the same mapping. With Proactive selected here, the chosen status lands in expect and after stays empty, inverting the intended 'stays in status' semantics.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-pool automation fires on absence of the status event instead of when the pool stays in that status for the within period.
findings.title: Work pool Proactive status stored in expect instead of after

findings.description: The status field is hardcoded to trigger.expect regardless of posture. FlowRunStateTriggerFields (flow-run-state-trigger-fields.tsx:24-25) and DeploymentStatusTriggerFields (deployment-status-trigger-fields.tsx:30-31) both use trigger.after for Proactive ('Stays in') and trigger.expect for Reactive. This component never writes trigger.after, so a Proactive selection is submitted as an expected event rather than a stay-in state.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive work-queue automation triggers on the status event not occurring, the opposite of the 'Stays in' behavior the user selected.
findings.title: Work queue Proactive status stored in expect instead of after

findings.description: ''.split('\n') returns [''] in JavaScript (verified with node), so lines.length > 0 is always true and the undefined branch is dead; clearing the textarea stores [''] and a trailing newline appends ''. The Zod schema accepts any string in expect, and the backend expects() only treats an empty expect set as match-any, so [''] matches no real event instead of meaning no expected events. Empty lines must be filtered before calling field.onChange.
findings.failureMode: Clearing the custom-events textarea submits expect=[''], creating a reactive automation that can never match any event.
findings.title: Custom trigger stores empty string as an expected event

findings.description: The diff flips compilerOptions.strict from true to false in tsconfig.app.json, weakening the type-checking enforcement that validate:types (tsc -b --noEmit) relies on and violating repository mandate 11 requiring strict mode. Nothing in the new components requires relaxed checking; they already guard optional values. Restore strict: true.
findings.failureMode: Null/undefined and implicit-any errors across the whole ui-v2 app pass type validation and surface as runtime crashes instead of compile-time failures.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled

findings.description: This is the only bare parseInt( in ui-v2/src; biome.json sets style/useNumberNamespace to error and CI runs biome ci (.github/workflows/ui-v2-checks.yml), so the check fails on this line. It also diverges from every sibling threshold field using Number(...): clearing the input gives parseInt('') === NaN (verified with node) instead of 0, and decimals are silently truncated. Use Number(e.target.value) like the other trigger fields.
findings.failureMode: The biome ci job fails on this file, and clearing the work-pool threshold stores NaN instead of following the sibling validation path.
findings.title: Bare parseInt violates Biome useNumberNamespace and yields NaN

findings.description: The guard `if rendered is not None and not isinstance(rendered, str)` exempts None, so `return rendered` returns None from a method declared `-> str` when the executor result has no "result" key. I verified this with a fake executor returning {} (render_template returned None) and with basedpyright and mypy, both reporting an incompatible `str | None` return at line 40, which fails the style CI type gates. TemplateTransformNode._run then calls len(rendered) at template_transform_node.py:69 inside a handler that only catches TemplateRenderError, so the node raises TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; the fix is to raise TemplateRenderError for any non-str rendered value, including None.
findings.failureMode: A missing or None "result" from the code executor escapes as None, failing type-check CI and crashing template-transform execution with TypeError on len() instead of a handled node failure.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing result

findings.description: Base used `if !gtk.exists()` and the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 still does, but line 243 uses `if gtk.exists()`. On a fresh tools directory the embedded linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is never written, yet bundle_project unconditionally passes `--plugin gtk` to linuxdeploy (lines 201-202). Fix to `if !gtk.exists()`.
findings.failureMode: First AppImage bundle on a clean machine fails in linuxdeploy because the GTK plugin script is missing.
findings.title: GTK plugin condition inverted, fresh installs never write it

findings.description: Base wrote the file first and then called set_permissions; line 312 now calls fs::set_permissions before fs::write on line 313. Every caller except the inverted GTK block is guarded by `!exists()`, so the path does not exist yet and set_permissions fails with ENOENT. Restore write-then-set_permissions order.
findings.failureMode: prepare_tools fails on first use for AppRun, linuxdeploy and plugin files, so AppImage bundling cannot proceed.
findings.title: Permissions set before file is written

findings.description: write_and_make_executable now returns Result<(), FileWriteError> at line 309, replacing std::io::Result. prepare_tools returns crate::Result<PathBuf> and uses `?` on this function (lines 232, 239, 259), but crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs has no From<FileWriteError> for crate::Error (only From<io::Error> and From<anyhow::Error>, which are not transitive). This is a `?` conversion (E0277) compile failure on Linux; return io::Result or add a proper conversion.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile for Linux targets.
findings.title: FileWriteError does not convert into crate::Error, breaking compilation

findings.description: Line 235 maps i686 to the linuxdeploy arch name and line 236 uses it for the local file, and base used that same variable in the download URL. Line 238 now interpolates raw `{arch}`, requesting linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage for 32-bit x86 builds instead of the mapped i386-style asset name used elsewhere (lines 25 and 139). Restore `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage builds fail to download linuxdeploy (404) and prepare_tools returns an error.
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL bypasses arch mapping

findings.description: Mandate 8 requires custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes. FileWriteError at line 286 derives only Debug and manually implements Display (line 291) and std::error::Error (line 300). Replace the manual impls with a thiserror derive (or keep std::io::Error, which crate::Error already converts from).
findings.failureMode: The new error type violates the repository thiserror mandate and is inconsistent with the crate error type in error.rs.
findings.title: Custom error enum does not use thiserror

findings.description: Running `rustfmt --check` on this file reports a single diff wrapping line 312, whose long set_permissions/map_err chain exceeds the project max_width=100 in rustfmt.toml. Mandate 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass. Reformat the chain as rustfmt specifies.
findings.failureMode: The cargo fmt --check CI gate fails on this file.
findings.title: Changed line is not rustfmt-formatted

findings.description: extractSlotFromKeysResult loops with j <= keys_result->numkeys (base used j < numkeys), so the final iteration reads keys[numkeys] and writes slot_buffer[numkeys] into a buffer allocated for only numkeys ints at line 1110. getKeysPrepareResult sizes the heap keys array to exactly numkeys, and the inline keysbuf entry past numkeys is a zeroed keyReference with pos 0, so a valid single-key cluster command hashes argv[0] as an extra key while larger key counts read/write out of bounds. Fix the bound to j < keys_result->numkeys (the slot_buffer itself is unnecessary).
findings.failureMode: Valid same-slot cluster commands are spuriously rejected as CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT, and with heap-sized key arrays the server corrupts the heap or crashes.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads and writes past key/slot arrays

findings.description: The new slot_buffer uses malloc at line 1110 and free at lines 1120 and 1124, violating AGENTS.md rule 2 requiring zmalloc/zfree outside zmalloc.c; server.h marks malloc/free deprecated for this reason. Verified by running make -C src cluster.o REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror", which fails with -Werror,-Wdeprecated-declarations errors on all three calls, also violating rule 4. Use zmalloc/zfree or remove the unused buffer entirely.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails to compile cluster.c, and the allocation bypasses Redis memory tracking.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free breaks zmalloc mandate and -Werror build

findings.description: Line 31 binds the status select to trigger.after when posture is Proactive, unlike the work-pool, work-queue, and custom components in this diff which always use trigger.expect. The backend EventTrigger uses expect for the expected events in both postures (Reactive responds to their presence, Proactive to their absence) and after only as the prerequisite event that starts the window; with expect left empty the backend's expects() matches any event. Selecting Proactive + Ready therefore creates after=["prefect.deployment.ready"] with no expected status, and switching posture also orphans the previously selected status in the other field so both can be submitted together. Fix: always bind the status select to trigger.expect.
findings.failureMode: A Proactive deployment-status automation does not expect the selected status event, so it evaluates against any event after the status instead of the absence/presence of that status and fires incorrectly or not at all.
findings.title: Proactive deployment status written to trigger.after instead of trigger.expect

findings.description: The diff changes "strict": true to "strict": false in tsconfig.app.json, which directly violates AGENTS.md rule 11 requiring strict mode enabled with the validate:types script (tsc -b --noEmit) in package.json. This weakens the type-checking enforcement for the whole ui-v2 app rather than fixing any type errors in the new components. Code with implicit any, unchecked null/undefined, or unsound assignments will now pass tsc -b --noEmit and the build. Fix: restore "strict": true and fix any resulting type errors in the new files.
findings.failureMode: validate:types and the production build silently accept type-unsafe code that strict checking would reject, allowing null/undefined defects to reach runtime as crashes.
findings.title: TypeScript strict mode disabled

findings.description:
Lines 38-39 split the textarea on "
" and guard only on lines.length > 0, but String.split never returns an empty array: "".split("
") is [""] and "a
".split("
") is ["a", ""] (verified by execution). Clearing the textarea therefore stores expect=[""] instead of undefined, and ending the input with a newline stores a trailing "" alongside the real events. The AutomationWizardSchema accepts any string array, so the empty event name is submitted and matches no real event. Fix: filter out empty (and whitespace-only) lines and pass undefined when none remain.
findings.failureMode: A cleared or trailing-newline custom trigger is submitted expecting an empty-string event that never occurs, so a Reactive automation never fires (and a Proactive one can fire spuriously).
findings.title: Custom trigger textarea stores empty-string expected events

findings.description: Line 78 uses the global parseInt(e.target.value) with no radix, while every sibling component in this diff (and the existing FlowRunStateTriggerFields) uses Number(e.target.value) and the rest of ui-v2 uses Number.parseInt(value, 10). ui-v2/biome.json sets the style rule useNumberNamespace to "error", which forbids the global parseInt, so biome check/lint fails on this line. parseInt also parses differently from Number, e.g. parseInt("1e3") is 1 instead of 1000 and parseInt("") is NaN (verified by execution). Fix: use Number(e.target.value) like the other trigger field components.
findings.failureMode: The biome lint gate errors on the global parseInt, and threshold values such as exponent-form number input are parsed to the wrong number.
findings.title: Global parseInt without radix for work-pool threshold

findings.description: prepare_tools returns crate::Result<PathBuf> (Result<T, crate::Error>) and uses `write_and_make_executable(...)?` at lines 232, 239, 245, 251 and 259, but the helper now returns Result<(), FileWriteError>. I grepped crates/tauri-bundler/src/error.rs: crate::Error has #[from] conversions for io::Error and others but no From<FileWriteError>, and a rustc probe of this shape fails with E0277 `the trait From<FileWriteError> is not implemented for Error`. The module is compiled under #[cfg(target_os = "linux")], so Linux builds of tauri-bundler fail. Fix by returning std::io::Result as before or adding a From conversion into crate::Error.
findings.failureMode: tauri-bundler fails to compile on Linux, blocking all AppImage bundling.
findings.title: FileWriteError does not convert to crate::Error, breaking Linux compilation

findings.description: The base code called fs::write then fs::set_permissions; the new code calls fs::set_permissions first. Every caller only invokes this helper when the target does not exist yet (e.g. `if !apprun.exists()`, `if !linuxdeploy.exists()`, `if !gstreamer.exists()`), and chmod on a nonexistent path returns NotFound. On a fresh tools directory the first call therefore errors before any bytes are written. Fix by writing the file first and setting mode 0o770 afterwards.
findings.failureMode: On a clean machine prepare_tools fails with a permissions NotFound error and no AppImage tools are installed.
findings.title: Permissions are set before the file is written, so first-time writes always fail

findings.description: The base code used `if !gtk.exists()` and the parallel gstreamer block at line 249 still uses `if !gstreamer.exists()`, but the GTK block was changed to `if gtk.exists()`. On a fresh tools directory linuxdeploy-plugin-gtk.sh is therefore never written, while bundle_project always passes `--plugin gtk` to linuxdeploy (lines 201-202). Fix by restoring `if !gtk.exists()` (or writing unconditionally).
findings.failureMode: linuxdeploy fails because the gtk plugin script is missing from the tools directory on first run.
findings.title: Inverted existence check prevents the GTK plugin from ever being installed on fresh setups

findings.description: Line 235 maps arch `i686` to linuxdeploy_arch and line 236 names the local file with that mapped value, and the base code also used linuxdeploy_arch in the download URL. The changed line uses `{arch}` in the URL, so for i686 targets the download requests linuxdeploy-i686.AppImage while the expected/installed artifact is the mapped name. For other arches the values coincide, which confines the breakage to i686. Fix by using `{linuxdeploy_arch}` in the URL as before.
findings.failureMode: i686 AppImage bundling fails to download linuxdeploy (wrong release asset name / 404).
findings.title: linuxdeploy download URL uses raw arch instead of the mapped linuxdeploy_arch

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 8 requires all custom error enums to use #[derive(thiserror::Error)] with #[error(...)] attributes and lists manual Display/Error implementations as the failure criterion. The new FileWriteError at lines 285-307 derives only Debug and hand-implements Display and std::error::Error. This is independent of the missing From conversion: adding that conversion alone would still leave the mandate violated. Fix by deriving thiserror::Error with #[error] messages, or by removing the custom type and returning io::Result.
findings.failureMode: The new error type violates the repository's mandatory error-handling convention and is rejected under the AGENTS.md compliance rules.
findings.title: Custom FileWriteError manually implements Display/Error instead of using thiserror

findings.description: AGENTS.md rule 3 requires `cargo fmt --all -- --check` to pass with rustfmt.toml (max_width=100). I ran the toolchain rustfmt in --check mode on this file and it reports a diff at line 312, rewrapping the 101-column set_permissions call onto two lines. No other hunk in the file produced a rustfmt diff. Fix by running cargo fmt on the file.
findings.failureMode: The required formatting gate `cargo fmt --all -- --check` fails on this file.
findings.title: Changed line 312 exceeds rustfmt max_width and fails cargo fmt --check

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now sets displayView to .readerModeLongPressAction instead of the base .readerMode. In BrowserViewController.handleDisplayActions, .readerMode calls toggleReaderMode() while .readerModeLongPressAction calls toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which creates a reading-list record; handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction already maps to the long-press display type. Restore displayView: .readerMode in handleShowReaderModeAction.
findings.failureMode: Tapping Reader Mode (showReaderMode) does not enter or exit Reader Mode and instead adds the page to the reading list.
findings.title: Reader Mode tap triggers reading-list long-press instead of toggling Reader Mode

findings.description: The base condition was (currentURL.isWebPage() && !currentURL.isReaderModeURL); the changed (isWebPage() || isReaderModeURL) no longer excludes Reader Mode URLs, which are http://localhost/reader-mode/page URLs and therefore also satisfy isWebPage(). When cancelEditMode runs while Reader Mode is active, the ToolbarAction now carries that internal URL, and AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction stores toolbarAction.url as the address-bar url instead of falling back to the existing state.url. Restore the && !isReaderModeURL condition.
findings.failureMode: Cancelling edit mode on a Reader Mode page puts the internal localhost reader-mode URL into address-bar state instead of the page URL.
findings.title: Cancel-edit now keeps the internal Reader Mode URL

findings.description: ReaderModeState.available means Reader Mode is not yet active and the tap will enable it, as the retained comment states, so the base returned true for .available and false otherwise (.active disables on tap). The changed switch returns false for .available and true by default, flipping isEnabled passed to toolbarTelemetry.readerModeButtonTapped. Restore .available: true and default: false.
findings.failureMode: Reader Mode button telemetry reports openings as not enabled and closings/other states as enabled, corrupting the enabled dimension.
findings.title: Reader Mode telemetry enabled flag is inverted

findings.description: The property was changed from private let gleanWrapper to internal let gleanWrapper, although it is only used inside ToolbarTelemetry and no caller in the diff needs direct access. This violates AGENTS.md Rule 11, which requires private access control for implementation details only used internally. Restore private let gleanWrapper.
findings.failureMode: Module-internal code can access and call the injected GleanWrapper directly, bypassing the ToolbarTelemetry facade and breaking the mandated encapsulation.
findings.title: ToolbarTelemetry exposes its private Glean wrapper

findings.description: This changed line requires '../email-service/email-event-storage', but that module was not renamed in this diff and still exists as ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/EmailEventStorage.js. A case-sensitive check against git ls-files finds no email-event-storage.js, and Node require.resolve for the new path fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Fix by reverting to '../email-service/EmailEventStorage' or renaming the target file in the same change.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on startup, breaking email analytics initialization.
findings.title: Broken require for email-event-storage (file not renamed)

findings.description: This changed line requires '../email-service/email-event-processor', but that module was not renamed in this diff and still exists as ghost/core/core/server/services/email-service/EmailEventProcessor.js. A case-sensitive check against git ls-files finds no email-event-processor.js, and Node require.resolve for the new path fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Fix by reverting to '../email-service/EmailEventProcessor' or renaming the target file in the same change.
findings.failureMode: EmailAnalyticsServiceWrapper.init() throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND on startup even after the preceding require is fixed, breaking email analytics initialization.
findings.title: Broken require for email-event-processor (file not renamed)

findings.description: This changed line requires '../../lib/magic-link/magic-link', but that module was not renamed in this diff and still exists as ghost/core/core/server/services/lib/magic-link/MagicLink.js. A case-sensitive check against git ls-files finds no magic-link.js in that directory, and Node require.resolve fails with MODULE_NOT_FOUND. Fix by reverting to '../../lib/magic-link/MagicLink' or renaming the target file in the same change.
findings.failureMode: Loading the Members API module throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND at startup, breaking member signup and authentication routes.
findings.title: Broken require for magic-link (file not renamed)

findings.description: The changed lines 1-4 and 6-10 in this file lost their terminating semicolons (for example line 1 is now `const {Router} = require('express')` with no semicolon), while the base version and the rest of the same block from line 12 onward keep them. Repository mandate 19 requires explicit semicolons at the end of all statements, so these nine changed lines violate it even though ASI makes them parse. Fix by restoring a semicolon at the end of each of lines 1-4 and 6-10.
findings.failureMode: The file fails the repository semicolon lint/mandate check for this file, blocking the lint gate despite parsing via ASI.
findings.title: Semicolons dropped from require statements

findings.description: handleShowReaderModeAction now returns displayView .readerModeLongPressAction instead of the base .readerMode, making it identical to handleAddToReadingListLongPressAction. BrowserViewController handles .readerMode with toggleReaderMode() but .readerModeLongPressAction with toggleReaderModeLongPressAction(), which adds the page to the reading list. Restoring .readerMode is the fix.
findings.failureMode: Tapping the Reader Mode toolbar button adds the page to the reading list instead of entering or exiting Reader Mode.
findings.title: Reader Mode tap routes to long-press action

findings.description: The base guard kept the tab URL only when isWebPage() && !isReaderModeURL; the new || form keeps it precisely for Reader Mode URLs (http://localhost/reader-mode/page, which isWebPage() also accepts). AddressBarState.handleCancelEditAction then stores toolbarAction.url over state.url, replacing the decoded displayURL that urlDidChange dispatches normally store with the raw internal Reader Mode URL.
findings.failureMode: Cancelling address-bar editing while in Reader Mode leaves address-bar state holding the internal localhost Reader Mode URL instead of preserving the page's display URL.
findings.title: cancelEditMode now admits Reader Mode URLs

findings.description: recordReaderModeTelemetry flips both branches of the base switch: .available now reports false despite its own comment that Reader Mode will be enabled after the tap, and the default branch (including .active, where a tap disables Reader Mode) now reports true. Grep of ReaderModeState confirms the available/active/unavailable cases, so every tap now records the opposite post-tap enabled value.
findings.failureMode: Reader Mode button telemetry records enabled exactly backwards, corrupting enable/disable counts for every tap.
findings.title: Reader Mode telemetry enabled flag inverted

findings.description: The changed line drops private from ToolbarTelemetry.gleanWrapper, violating AGENTS.md rule 11 that implementation-detail properties be private. A grep for external .gleanWrapper access and ToolbarTelemetry call sites shows no caller outside the struct needs the wrapper, so nothing justifies the widening; the base private declaration should be restored.
findings.failureMode: Any module code can now reach the telemetry wrapper directly, bypassing the ToolbarTelemetry API and breaking the repository access-control mandate.
findings.title: gleanWrapper access widened from private to internal

findings.description: The local GetAvailableSlotsResponse copy declares fromUser.id as string, while the source contract IFromUser in packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts declares id: number and the slots service sets it from user.id. useAvailableSlots now returns this local type, and BookerPlatformWrapper passes that schedule to Booker, whose schedule prop expects the trpc-derived IGetAvailableSlots shape with a numeric id. A standalone tsc check confirms string is not assignable to number for this property. Fix: change fromUser.id to number.
findings.failureMode: The atoms schedule result is no longer type-compatible with the Booker schedule prop, failing type-checking on the main Booker rendering path.
findings.title: SlotInfo.fromUser.id typed as string instead of number

findings.description: GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn declares availability.days as string[], but the Prisma Availability model defines days as Int[] and the original list handler return carried number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes these schedules to getScheduleListItemData in packages/lib/schedules/transformers/getScheduleListItemData.ts, whose Schedule type requires days: number[]. A standalone tsc check confirms string[] is not assignable to number[] here. Fix: change days to number[].
findings.failureMode: Type-checking fails where the schedules list is transformed for display, and typed consumers mishandle weekday numbers as strings.
findings.title: Availability days typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: The diff widens the atoms noRestrictedImports rule from @calcom/trpc/react to all of @calcom/trpc, but packages/platform/atoms/connect/conferencing-apps/ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx and packages/platform/atoms/selected-calendars/wrappers/SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx still import QueryCell from @calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell. Running biome lint on those files at head reports two noRestrictedImports errors with the new message. Fix: migrate those two QueryCell imports off @calcom/trpc or keep a scoped exception until they are migrated.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint, enforced with error-on-warnings, fails on unchanged atoms files, blocking commits and CI for the package.
findings.title: Broadened Biome trpc ban breaks lint on two remaining atoms imports

findings.description: The copied Slot type declares userIds as string[], but the deleted original in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/types.ts declared number[] and packages/features/schedules/lib/slots.ts produces numeric userIds. Booker consumers receive this type through onTimeslotsLoaded (Record<string, Slot[]>), so code comparing slot.userIds against numeric user ids no longer type-checks, and code written against the new string type fails to match runtime numbers. Fix: restore userIds?: number[].
findings.failureMode: Atoms Booker consumers get a wrong public type for slot userIds, breaking numeric id comparisons against the values actually delivered at runtime.
findings.title: Slot.userIds changed from number[] to string[]

findings.description: The new validator only checks that input is an object with a non-empty name, then returns the whole record cast as CreateScheduleInput without checking schedule or eventTypeId. The Zod schema it stands in for (ZCreateInputSchema) validated schedule as arrays of {start: Date, end: Date} and eventTypeId as a number, and repository mandate 5 requires Zod-backed typed schemas rather than hand-rolled casts. A caller passing {name: 'x', eventTypeId: 'abc', schedule: 'bad'} receives it as valid CreateScheduleInput. Fix: validate schedule and eventTypeId (ideally with a Zod schema) before returning, or remove the unused validator.
findings.failureMode: Invalid schedule payloads pass client validation and reach the schedules API or downstream Date handling instead of being rejected at the boundary.
findings.title: validateCreateScheduleInput casts unchecked fields as valid input

findings.description: Both failure paths throw plain Error objects (lines 40 and 46). Repository mandate 10 requires custom errors extending a base error type with typed codes and context, and explicitly lists throwing generic Error objects as a failure criterion. Callers cannot programmatically distinguish these validation failures or map them to a status code. Fix: throw a typed error from the repository error hierarchy at both sites.
findings.failureMode: Validation failures surface as uncategorized errors with no code or status, defeating structured error handling by callers.
findings.title: Validator throws generic Error instead of a typed error class

findings.description: Lines 39-46 use single-quoted strings while biome.json configures javascript.formatter.quoteStyle as double, per mandate 3. Running biome format on this file at head reports a formatter error and would rewrite all four string literals. Fix: reformat the function with Biome so the literals use double quotes.
findings.failureMode: The Biome format check fails on this file, blocking the formatting gate for the change.
findings.title: Single quotes in new validator violate Biome double-quote formatting

findings.description: The override now blocks all '@calcom/trpc/**' for packages/platform/atoms, but ConferencingAppsViewPlatformWrapper.tsx:12 and SelectedCalendarsSettingsPlatformWrapper.tsx:6 still import QueryCell from '@calcom/trpc/components/QueryCell', which was allowed under the old '@calcom/trpc/react' pattern. Running biome 2.3.10 lint on those files reports 2 lint/style/noRestrictedImports errors and exits 1. Either those imports must be migrated or the ban must not be widened yet.
findings.failureMode: Biome lint/pre-commit fails on the atoms package, blocking CI and commits.
findings.title: Widened trpc import ban breaks lint on remaining QueryCell imports

findings.description: The copied GetAvailabilityListHandlerReturn declares availability.days as string[], but the source list handler returns Prisma Availability rows whose days column is Int[] (schema.prisma:941), and getScheduleListItemData requires days: number[]. ListSchedulesPlatformWrapper passes each schedule from useAtomGetAllSchedules to getScheduleListItemData, so the atoms typecheck now rejects that call. Change days to number[].
findings.failureMode: Atoms TypeScript build fails where schedules are passed to getScheduleListItemData, and consumers mistype numeric weekdays as strings.
findings.title: Availability days typed as string[] instead of number[]

findings.description: The new SlotInfo copies IGetAvailableSlots but declares fromUser.id as string, while IFromUser (packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts:176-179) declares id: number and toUser.id is correctly copied as number. EventTypeCalendarViewComponent passes useAvailableSlots data (now GetAvailableSlotsResponse) to useAvailableTimeSlots, which expects IGetAvailableSlots, so the assignment is structurally incompatible. Change fromUser.id to number.
findings.failureMode: Atoms TypeScript build fails assigning available-slots data to useAvailableTimeSlots, and consumers mistype the OOO user id.
findings.title: SlotInfo fromUser.id typed as string instead of number

findings.description: The deleted Slot in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/slots/types.ts declared userIds?: number[], matching server code that fills it from numeric user.id values (slots util and features/schedules/lib/slots.ts), but the copied type declares string[]. This is a transcription change to a supposedly moved type, not the documented relocation. Restore number[].
findings.failureMode: Consumers of onTimeslotsLoaded/Slot fail to compile when assigning numeric user ids or wrongly treat runtime numbers as strings.
findings.title: Moved Slot type changes userIds from number[] to string[]

findings.description: The new validator only checks that name is a non-empty string, then returns 'data as CreateScheduleInput' without validating schedule or eventTypeId. It replaces the ZCreateInputSchema contract (zod array of {start: Date, end: Date} and numeric eventTypeId), so input like {name:'Work', schedule:'bad', eventTypeId:'abc'} is returned as valid typed input and malformed data reaches the create-schedule POST instead of a validation error. It also throws generic Error objects rather than following the separated Zod schema pattern.
findings.failureMode: Callers trusting the validator send malformed schedule payloads that fail server-side instead of being rejected at validation.
findings.title: validateCreateScheduleInput casts unchecked fields to CreateScheduleInput

findings.description: Lines 39-46 use single-quoted strings while biome.json sets javascript.formatter.quoteStyle to 'double'. Running biome 2.3.10 format on this file exits 1 and reports the formatter would rewrite these lines. Reformat the file with Biome.
findings.failureMode: Biome format checks and lint-staged formatting fail on the new file.
findings.title: New validator uses single quotes violating Biome double-quote format

findings.description: In template_renderer.py render_template does result.get("result") and only rejects non-strings when rendered is not None, so a missing key or {"result": None} from an injected CodeExecutor returns None despite the -> str contract. TemplateTransformNode._run then calls len(rendered) at template_transform_node.py:69 inside a try that only catches TemplateRenderError, so it raises TypeError instead of returning a FAILED NodeRunResult; I reproduced this with a stub executor returning {} and {"result": None}, both returning None then failing len() while an int result correctly raises TemplateRenderError. Fix the guard to reject any non-string including None (if not isinstance(rendered, str): raise TemplateRenderError(...)).
findings.failureMode: A code executor response without a string result makes TemplateTransformNode._run raise TypeError on len(None) instead of returning a clean FAILED result.
findings.title: Renderer returns None for missing result, crashing node on len()

findings.description: Line 106 moves the public macOS pool to vmImage macOS-15 and line 167 now claims 'Use XCode 16.4.0', but the adjacent unchanged script at line 166 still runs 'sudo xcode-select -s /Applications/Xcode_15.2.0.app/Contents/Developer'. The macOS-15 hosted image ships Xcode 16.x, not Xcode 15.2, so xcode-select points at a developer directory that does not exist and exits non-zero. The script path must be updated to the Xcode 16.4 app installed on that image.
findings.failureMode: Public macOS CI jobs fail at the xcode-select step before the build starts.
findings.title: macOS public job selects Xcode 15.2 on macOS-15 image

findings.description: The BUILD002 error condition now also requires '$(AspNetCorePatchVersion)' == '1', whereas the base required only a servicing build with unused baseline package references. docs/BuildErrors.md states BUILD002 appears in servicing builds, which should not change references between assemblies or packages, with no first-patch exception, and nothing in the new code re-establishes the check for later patches. In a 10.0.2 servicing build (AspNetCorePatchVersion=2), removing a BaselinePackageReference from a shipping package leaves UnusedBaselinePackageReference non-empty but no longer produces BUILD002.
findings.failureMode: A breaking package-reference removal in a 10.0.2 or later servicing update builds silently instead of failing with BUILD002.
findings.title: BUILD002 servicing reference check disabled after first patch

findings.description: The diff replaces the file-scoped declaration 'namespace Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components.E2ETests.ServerExecutionTests;' with a block-scoped namespace at line 16 plus opening and closing braces. AGENTS.md rule 2 mandates file-scoped namespace declarations in all C# files and .editorconfig sets csharp_style_namespace_declarations = file_scoped with IDE0161 at warning severity. Restoring the semicolon-terminated file-scoped namespace and removing the added braces fixes the violation.
findings.failureMode: The changed file violates the mandatory file-scoped namespace rule and reports IDE0161 for this file.
findings.title: Test file reverts to block-scoped namespace

findings.description: The loop at src/cluster.c:1112 uses j <= keys_result->numkeys, so it executes for j==numkeys. At that iteration keys_result->keys[j] is past the valid key references and slot_buffer[j] at line 1115 writes past the numkeys-element buffer allocated at line 1110. For a single-key cluster command it hashes argv[keys[1].pos] from uninitialized/out-of-bounds data, producing a spurious CLUSTER_CROSSSLOT or heap corruption instead of the key's slot.
findings.failureMode: Any cluster command with keys can crash, corrupt the heap, or be wrongly rejected as cross-slot.
findings.title: Off-by-one loop reads and writes past key/slot arrays

findings.description: Line 1110 uses malloc() and lines 1120 and 1124 use free() for slot_buffer, contrary to the repository mandate to use zmalloc/zfree outside zmalloc.c. Compiling with make -C src cluster.o REDIS_CFLAGS="-Werror" fails with three deprecated-declaration errors for malloc/free declared in src/server.h. Remove the unused slot_buffer, or allocate it with zmalloc and release both paths with zfree.
findings.failureMode: The mandated -Werror build fails, and the allocation bypasses Redis used_memory tracking.
findings.title: Direct malloc/free violates zmalloc mandate and breaks -Werror build
